messages:
Maya Patel: heads-up, brought a new HF GPT-like model into Redwood Dedicated and seeing streaming responses cut off early when the model emits multiple EOS-like tokens. Pretty sure it's a conversion/stop handling mismatch.
Alex Chen: can you paste a minimal repro? platform or private?
Maya Patel: dedicated cluster, quantized int4. repro is simple: prompt that causes the model to output a sentence then a signature token and then a blank line token. Streaming callback receives data then stops immediately after the first EOS token id.
Jin Park: same symptoms we've seen elsewhere when token id mapping changed during hf->redwood conversion. Did you check tokenizer special_tokens_map?
Maya Patel: yup. tokenizer config has both "eos_token": "", and a legacy "pad_token": "" mapped. config.json shows: 
```json
{"bos_token":"","eos_token":"","pad_token":"","special_tokens_map":{}}
```
But model weights came with an extra sentinel token id 50257 labeled "</s>" in the HF vocab file. Redwood's converter seems to canonicalize to 50256 for eos which causes duplicate sentinel handling.
Priya Sinha: interesting — we also saw streaming clipping with repeated empty-string tokens in chat templates. which API did you call? streaming completion or chat?
Maya Patel: chat streaming with system/user turns. client-side got CHUNK, then a final chunk immediately when it saw token id 50256. However the model continued producing tokens on the server for ~120ms according to logs.
Ramon Torres: can you attach the server token trace? infra-bot pulled the logs: 
```
[1760912345.123] token_stream: 345 67 89 50256 23 50256 48 10
[1760912345.245] send_stream_chunk: up to token idx 4 (id 50256) -> flush and close stream
```
Maya Patel: exactly. converter callstack: hf_loader -> convert_token_map -> write_config. I suspect convert_token_map treats any token mapped to eos_token string as canonical EOS and sets a stop-on-first-token flag.
Alex Chen: if converter sets "stop_on_eos": true globally that would cause Redwood runtime to terminate streaming on first matched EOS token id. That would ignore cases where EOS is used inside answer (multiple eos) or used as separator between segments.
Jin Park: quick workaround: add an explicit stop sequence in the request to exclude that short token, e.g., stop=["\n\n"] or set stop_words to the multi-token sequence. But that's brittle.
Priya Sinha: we should reproduce with python snippet to print token ids and emulate stream handler. Maya, can you run this small test and paste output?
Maya Patel: ran it. snippet: 
```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForCausalLM
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('local-model')
print(tok.encode('Hello\n\n'))
```
Output: [15496, 13, 13, 50256, 50257] 
So HF tokenizer yields both 50256 and 50257 depending on piecewise encoding. Sequence contains two eos-like ids.
Ramon Torres: converter should preserve full id set and not dedupe or remap silently. If it remaps 50257->50256 and sets stop_on_first_eos, that explains early termination.
Alex Chen: action items: 1) Maya to capture full converter config.json that was written by the onboarding tool, 2) Jin to add a unit test in converter that asserts no remap of distinct eos-like ids, 3) Priya to update streaming runtime to consider stop sequences as sequence-level matches rather than first-token-match when 'stop_sequences' configured.
Maya Patel: uploaded converter_config.json to the onboarding ticket. Quick temporary mitigation: set runtime option "treat_multiple_eos_as_inband": true which keeps streaming open until a configurable count or explicit stop-sequence matched. Works for our use-case.
Priya Sinha: good. for long-term fix we should also make tokenizer->redwood mapping deterministic and emit a warning when multiple distinct tokens are used as EOS in HF artifacts.
Jin Park: I'll prototype a failing test: feed vocab with duplicate labels for eos and assert converter preserves both ids and sets no global stop flag.
Alex Chen: thanks — let's also log token ids in runtime for 1% of requests so we can detect other models with mixed EOS/"</s>" behavior.
Maya Patel: filed bug: RH-2314 with reproducer + logs + suggested config tweak. tagging @infra for prioritization. :bug:
Ramon Torres: noted, moving to high priority. infra-bot: created incident RH-2314 and linked logs.
infra-bot: Incident RH-2314 created by Ramon Torres. Priority: P2. Links: https://internal/infra/incidents/RH-2314
Alex Chen: once converter test is in place, I'll coordinate a small patch to runtime stop matching to prefer longest stop sequence first (sequence-aware), not first token. That should fix streaming false positives.
Priya Sinha: also check quantization path — lowering precision can change tokenization in some models if tokenizer normalization differs. add tokenizer serialization check to quantization CI.
Maya Patel: thanks all — will monitor. if anyone wants the reproducer prompt: "Write a short email signature followed by two blank lines and then 'P.S.'"
Alex Chen: solid repro. tagging eng-releases if we need a hotfix deploy. :rocket:
